findings.title: S8's stale-rename check cannot happen: an agent's rename is a ghost and never moves the authored revision
findings.claim: In the design as written, a person's write can only go stale against another person's applied write or an auto-enabled decision effect. Agent B's rename is a ghost. Ghosts are not applied, so they never bump rev(target, field). The tab's rename made over B's rename therefore applies with no conflict, and the node ends up with the tab's name. S8 expects the reverse.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:368: "rev(target, field) is the seq of the last applied event that set it". architecture.md:328 and DR-4: any agent edit is a ghost, excluded until a person's review accept. The write-path diagram (architecture.md:262-268) applies the conflict test only to revisions, so a ghost never makes a later write stale. feature_list.json S8 asserts: "the tab's stale rename returned stale_write, is stored as a conflict with base, theirs and yours, raised one person card, and the node still has B's name" (B = agent:bbbbbbbb:chat). KICKOFF S8, tier A: "a stale write becomes a diff rather than a merge".
findings.failure_scenario: The S8 harness runs B's `planroom edit rename storefront:dir:src/cart` as agent:bbbbbbbb:chat, which is stored as a ghost. The tab then renames with an older base. store::commit finds no applied revision above base, so the tab's edit applies. The reply is ok, not stale_write, and no card is raised. s08_concurrency.rs::stale_write_becomes_a_diff fails, so tier A S8 fails. The 'agent stale write' half can only be produced by a person write landing between an agent's read and its write. Nothing in the harness arranges that.
findings.proposed_fix: Choose one model and write it down in DR-5 and DR-7. (a) Make the S8 stale write person against person: two distinct person writers, such as the tab and an Artifact or second-device person (this needs correctness-2's fix), or the tab against a mod button press. Then rewrite the S8 harness and assertion to use that pair. (b) Alternatively, define a ghost-overlay revision, so that an agent's ghost on a field gives a person's later edit to that field a 'pending proposal' conflict. Either way, add a kernel cas.rs case that pins the chosen semantics.

findings.title: Person identity is too coarse: every person surface is one actor, so a stale write from one surface silently overwrites another (last writer wins)
findings.claim: The canvas cookie, the mod's button presses and a TTY all resolve to the same actor, person:<os-user>. All non-TTY Bash callers without PLANROOM_ACTOR resolve to agent:cli. The conflict test exempts writes by the same actor ("An actor never conflicts with its own later writes"). So two canvas tabs on two devices, or the pane and a tab, can overwrite each other's user-authored fields with stale bases and get no conflict. The implementer, the curator and every other session's Bash agent share one identity, so any of them can reject another's ghosts.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:380 (person:<os-user> for a TTY, the person key, or the canvas cookie); 382 (agent:cli for any no-TTY CLI call); 403-410 ("written by a different actor ... An actor never conflicts with its own later writes"); DR-5. KICKOFF R10: "canvas tabs on several devices ... User-authored state is never last-writer-wins"; principle 1: "Never lose or overwrite what someone did."
findings.failure_scenario: The laptop tab renders seq 40. The pane renames cart to 'Bag' at seq 41 (a person press). The tab, still showing seq 40, renames it to 'Basket' with base 40. rev=41 > base=40, but both writes are person:sridhar, so the tab's edit applies and 'Bag' is overwritten with no card. In the same way, a curator agent (agent:cli) can reject an implementer's ghosts, because both count as 'its own ghosts'.
findings.proposed_fix: Run the conflict test on a writer instance, not the actor: {actor, surface, client_id}, where client_id is the canvas tab ID, the mod session ID or the TTY pid. Alternatively, drop the same-actor exemption and rely on clients advancing their base from every write reply. Give Bash agents a required identity: the skills and agent definitions pass PLANROOM_ACTOR=agent:<agentId>:<role> (the mod knows agentId), and agent:cli writes are refused with an `actor_required` error. Add a cas.rs case: two tabs of one person conflict.

findings.title: The reconciler's change units and per-commit fact delta are undefined, and on the S4 CI path they misattribute or miss the planted regression
findings.claim: Three things are missing. Nothing stores 'last reconciled head', since there is no table, no event and reconcile is derived on read. Facts exist only for head snapshots, so no per-commit 'fact delta' exists. Merge commits are not handled. On the S4 CI path, `git merge --no-ff teammates` creates merge commits in storefront and worker. The audit commit's parent is pre-hand-off main, where worker -> orders-db already held through db.py and compose. A delta taken against the commit's own parent therefore shows no rule break, and a first-parent delta puts the break on 'Merge branch teammates'. The hand-off's own `merge --no-ff planroom/KEY` commit sits on main, not on the hand-off branch, so rule 5 can classify it as unplanned. Because the window is 'since the last scan', a regression also drops out of the reconciliation at the next scan of that repo.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:933 ("Change units are the commits between each repo's last reconciled head and its current head ... Each carries ... its fact delta"); 936 (regression = a change unit whose fact delta breaks a rule met before it); 940 (unplanned = a change unit not on a hand-off branch). Store schema at architecture.md:431-455 has no reconcile state; DR-2 says reconciliation classes are never stored. feature_list.json S4 step: "git -C $OUT/worker merge --no-ff teammates". Fixture: worker/10-audit-rows touches only worker/main.py and worker/audit.py on branch teammates, which starts from pre-hand-off main. TRUTH scenarios.S4.reconciliation_after_merges expects exactly done with regressions [worker-audit-db-write], storefront-gift-wrap unplanned, and worker-audit-db-write as a regression, matched by commit subject.
findings.failure_scenario: After the teammates merges, reconcile sees four candidate units: the gift-wrap commit, the storefront merge commit, the audit commit and the worker merge commit. Two outcomes are likely. (a) The regression goes to 'Merge branch teammates', so the planted subject is unplanned or unclassified. (b) The merge commits come out as extra unplanned items. Either way reconciliation_after_merges fails, and with it tier A S4 step 4. Later, any new worker commit followed by a rescan removes the regression from every view.
findings.proposed_fix: Specify the algorithm. Take the delta from the previous reconciled snapshot to the current head snapshot of the workspace link plus each repo. Attribute each changed fact to the non-merge commits in `git log --no-merges prev..head` whose touched files intersect the fact's evidence paths. Ignore merge commits, and also hand-off merge commits identified by the second parent planroom/KEY. Persist the outcome as a `reconcile` body on the scan event: per-repo reconciled head, item classes, and the regression's `against`. That makes classes and 'stays done' stable across later scans and makes the result independent of scan timing. Add fixture tests with --no-ff merges and a branch based on an older main.

findings.title: An accepted ghost or a resolved conflict applies at its original seq, so an edit made in between silently overrides the person's choice
findings.claim: The fold applies edits by effective status in seq order. A review accept changes status only, so the accepted edit keeps its old position. If any applied write to the same field falls between the proposal or conflict and the accept, it still wins in the fold. The person's acceptance, or 'Use yours', then has no visible effect, and nothing is reported. The accept is also never checked for staleness against fields that changed since the proposal.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:359: "Apply every edit with effective status Applied ... in seq order". architecture.md:350: status changes only through review and undo events. architecture.md:368: rev is the seq of the last applied event (ambiguous for an accepted ghost: its own seq, or the review's?). architecture.md:410: "Choosing 'yours' is a review accept that re-applies the edit with a fresh base", but no new edit event is defined. KICKOFF principle 1 ("Never lose or overwrite what someone did") and R10.
findings.failure_scenario: Claude proposes rename N to 'Basket' as a ghost at seq 50. Bob renames N to 'Bag' on the canvas at seq 60. Carol taps 'Accept 5 proposals' at seq 70. The fold applies 50, then 60, so N stays 'Bag', while the card reports the proposals accepted. A second case: a conflict stored at seq 12 (yours) over seq 11 (theirs), then another write at 13, then 'Use yours' at 15. The fold order 11, 12, 13 drops the person's resolution.
findings.proposed_fix: Make acceptance and conflict resolution write a new `edit` that copies the fields, with base equal to the accepting view's seq and cause set to the reviewed event. Run the normal field-level compare-and-set on it, so an accept over a newer revision becomes a three-way card instead of a silent no-op. Keep review events for the audit trail. Add cas.rs cases: an accept after an intervening write, and a resolution after an intervening write.

findings.title: The 'code, not prose' rule makes required alert evidence (a Go comment) unreachable
findings.claim: TRUTH requires orders/internal/http/middleware.go:26 as evidence for the OrdersHighErrorRate alert. That line is a `//` comment that links the OTel counter `orders_http_requests` to the Prometheus name `orders_http_requests_total`. The extractor contract forbids taking facts or evidence from comments, and no extractor or linker produces evidence from comment text. Full evidence recall is the stated bar, so the observability answer cannot match the truth.
findings.evidence: TRUTH questions.observability.alerts[0].evidence[2]: {path: orders/internal/http/middleware.go, line 26, contains: "// Prometheus exporter publishes them as orders_http_requests_total and"}. architecture.md:513 ("Code extractors take string literals and calls from syntax nodes, never from comments or docstrings"); contracts.md:536 (same rule); architecture.md:1192 ("every truth evidence item must appear ... Full evidence recall is the bar"). feature_list S2 compares TRUTH.questions.observability (alerts). This is the only comment line among the truth's evidence (checked by scanning every `contains`).
findings.failure_scenario: `planroom ask observability --json` returns the alert with the alerts.yml lines and the middleware.go:30 counter. The comparator does not find middleware.go:26, so observability_matches_truth fails and tier A S2 fails. The only way out today is an infeasibility record, which the design does not plan for.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a narrowly scoped evidence source in the observability pack: a declarative extractor for comment lines that mention a known metric name (an exact token match of a `metric` node's exported name). It attaches that line as evidence to the metric node or the `watches` edge, at lower confidence, and never creates relations. Also specify the OTel-to-Prometheus name mapping (add `_total` to counters, add a unit suffix) that the `telemetry` linker needs to join orders_http_requests to the alert's selector. Then restate the 'code, not prose' rule as applying to relation creation only.

findings.title: No extractor reads CHANGELOG versions, and evidence-or-nothing drops git-only facts (tags, commits, co-change)
findings.claim: The stale-version truth requires orders/CHANGELOG.md:7 as evidence for orders' latest version. Orders is Go and has no manifest version. No pack declares a changelog extractor. The release pack gets versions only from manifests and tags. A version or tag read from git refs has no file line, so under 'every fact carries at least one Evidence whose contains is the exact source line ... drops any that fail' tag nodes are dropped at ingest. So are commit nodes, co_change edges and owned_by edges. The stale answer for platform -> orders then either can't be computed or lacks required evidence, and the history lens is empty.
findings.evidence: TRUTH questions.stale_versions.stale[1].evidence[1] {orders/CHANGELOG.md, line 7, "## [1.5.0] - 2026-09-22"}; TRUTH repos.*.version_evidence are all CHANGELOG headings. architecture.md:512 (evidence or nothing, verified against the blob's line index); 681 (release pack: "gh_workflow release triggers, manifests' versions; deploys linker"); 554 (deploys joins "compose images, repo manifests and tags"); 567 (git tier emits co-change, ownership, churn); 312 (commits are Code-level nodes). Evidence.line is a required u32 (contracts.md, Graph model).
findings.failure_scenario: `planroom ask stale --json` reports platform on acme/orders 1.4.0 against latest 1.5.0. It takes the version from tag v1.5.0, whose fact has no line evidence and is dropped, so orders has no version and the comparison is skipped. If the fact survives, it still lacks the CHANGELOG.md:7 item. stale_versions_match_truth fails, so tier A S2 fails. Separately, `map --lens history` is empty for every repo.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a `changelog` built-in or declarative extractor to the release pack (Keep a Changelog `## [x.y.z]` headings) that sets each repo's `version` with line evidence, and prefer it over tags when both agree. Define a second evidence variant for git-derived facts, `Evidence::Ref {commit, ref}` or `{commit, path}`, verified against `git cat-file` or `for-each-ref` instead of a line index. Keep the 'exact line' rule for file-based facts.

findings.title: 'Live within 1 s' is measured when a frame arrives, not when the view updates; a trailing debounce never fires under load, and the refresh read can trigger a full rescan
findings.claim: The canvas refetches after 100 ms with no new frame, and the mod after 250 ms. Both are trailing debounces with no maximum wait. While writes keep arriving faster than that (S8: 600 writes plus retries from two agents), neither view refetches until the load stops. The mod's refresh runs `planroom focus`, a one-shot command that does the freshness check and refolds from scratch, and rescans any repo whose HEAD moved. So a pane update can wait on a multi-second scan. The S8 gate measures only commit-to-SSE and commit-to-watch frame latency, so it passes while every surface shows stale state.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:240 ("After 250 ms of quiet the mod runs planroom focus --json"); 1048 ("the canvas debounces 100 ms, the mod 250 ms"); 238 ("Each command first checks freshness ... rescans what moved"); performance table: "Commit to stream p99 under 1 s". feature_list S8 assert: "commit-to-SSE and commit-to-watch latency p99 under 1 s". KICKOFF R10 ("every surface updates live") and S8 ("live updates arrive within 1 s").
findings.failure_scenario: During the S8 run, agent A writes every 30 to 60 ms. The canvas never sees 100 ms of quiet, so the tab doesn't refetch until the run ends. The claim badge and B's rename appear seconds late. The pane behaves the same. In a live session, after `handoff merge` moves two HEADs, the debounced `focus` runs an inline rescan of worker and platform before it can redraw.
findings.proposed_fix: Use leading-edge plus trailing debounce with a maximum wait, such as 300 ms (canvas) and 500 ms (mod), so a refresh always lands within 1 s. Have `focus` and other refresh reads skip inline rescans when a live process holds or can take the `scan:REPO` lease, and return the current snapshot with `meta.stale_repos` instead. Change the S8 and S13 gates to measure commit-to-rendered (a DOM marker for the tab, and `planroom.pane` seq in $.state for the mod) under the S8 load.

findings.title: 'What's unmonitored?' would include otel-collector, prometheus and grafana, because no kind or prop separates observability infrastructure from runtime containers
findings.claim: The `unmonitored` question filters 'runtime containers with no incoming watches'. The code pack's container kinds are service, datastore, queue, library and tooling. Nothing classifies compose services such as otel-collector, prometheus and grafana as observability infrastructure (TRUTH kind 'observability'), and nothing says how redis becomes `queue` and postgres becomes `datastore`. The compose extractor would make these code.service nodes with no alert, so the answer has 7 containers instead of 4.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:652 and 663 (the filter over 'runtime containers'); 678 (code pack kinds); 680 (observability pack kinds: alert, dashboard, panel, metric, collector_pipeline; no container kind); 621 (services with no repo sit under the workspace; kind unstated). TRUTH questions.unmonitored.answer = [storefront, worker, redis, orders-db], with out_of_scope.observability_infrastructure = [otel-collector, prometheus, grafana]; TRUTH containers lists their kind as "observability". feature_list S2 compares "the four containers; monitored; out_of_scope".
findings.failure_scenario: `planroom ask unmonitored --json` returns storefront, worker, redis, orders-db, otel-collector, prometheus and grafana. unmonitored_matches_truth fails, so tier A S2 fails.
findings.proposed_fix: Have the compose extractor set a `role` prop from declared, testable image rules: postgres/mysql gives datastore; redis/rabbitmq gives queue; otel-collector, prometheus and grafana give observability. Put those rules in the code and observability packs as data, and have the observability pack contribute an `observability.infra` kind or prop through them. Define 'runtime container' in the `unmonitored` question as kinds {service, datastore, queue} with role != observability, and cover it in the pack conformance kit.

findings.title: Inline freshness rescans bypass the duty leases; concurrent scans collide on snapshot uniqueness, and leases have no fencing
findings.claim: A one-shot command that sees HEAD move rescans inline. A live `watch` may be rescanning the same repo under `scan:REPO` at the same moment. Both insert a snapshot with the same (repo, commit_id, purpose, packs_hash), so the second hits the UNIQUE constraint unless it upserts, and two scan events land. Leases are 30 s rows with no fencing token checked at commit. A paused holder, such as a laptop asleep, can commit duty output after another process took the lease over, which duplicates decision events and their effect edits.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:161 (duties under leases; with no live process, the work runs in 'the next command's freshness check'); 238 (every command rescans what moved); store schema at architecture.md:439-441: UNIQUE (repo, commit_id, purpose, packs_hash); leases(name, holder, expires_at), with no epoch.
findings.failure_scenario: After `handoff merge`, the mod's watch duty and the test's `planroom diff --intended` both rescan worker. One gets a constraint error, which shows up as an `internal` error envelope, or two scan events for one commit. A slow decide duty whose lease expired writes a second `decision` event and a second `put_edge` effect for the same input hash.
findings.proposed_fix: Have inline rescans take the same `scan:REPO` lease, or wait for a running holder up to a bound and then reuse its snapshot. Make snapshot insert idempotent (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, then select). Add a lease epoch that is checked inside the committing transaction. Derive decision-event idem from (kind, kind_version, subject, input_hash), so a duplicate run replays.

findings.title: `handoff merge` is not crash-atomic across repos, and the order of the git merges and the store event is unspecified
findings.claim: The preflight guards against merge conflicts, not against the process dying (a mod reload killing the process.run child, SIGKILL, or a disk error) between the per-repo `git merge` calls. The design also doesn't say whether the `merged` hand-off event commits before or after the git merges. Either order can leave the repos and the store disagreeing ('nothing is ever half-merged' is claimed). A retry with the same idem either replays a 'merged' reply over unmerged repos, or re-runs merges with no record of which repos are already done.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:984 ("Only if every repo passes does it run git merge --no-ff planroom/KEY in each ... so nothing is ever half-merged across repos"); DR-8 replay semantics (the stored reply is returned for the same idem); mod-api §7 (spawned children die on reload).
findings.failure_scenario: Merge succeeds in worker, then the process is killed before platform. If the event was committed first, the store says merged and reconcile runs on half the change. If not, the retry's preflight sees worker already merged, and the result depends on how that case is handled.
findings.proposed_fix: Write a `handoff merging` step event with the planned per-repo target commits before touching git. Merge each repo, recording each result. Commit `merged` at the end. On restart or retry, resume from the recorded per-repo state: skip a repo whose HEAD already contains planroom/KEY, and otherwise continue. Add a crash test that kills the process between repos.

findings.title: Derived idempotency keys merge intentional repeats, and multi-event commands have no per-event key rule
findings.claim: With no explicit key, idem is sha256(actor, command, args, base). An agent that reuses a base it read earlier and repeats a write after an undo (hide, undo, hide) gets the first reply back as a replay, so the second hide never happens. Commands that write several events (`edit group` is a put plus two parent sets; a scan writes one event per repo; a decision writes its record plus effect edits) need several UNIQUE idem values, and no derivation is specified. So a replay may return only part of the reply.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:416 (the derived key); 349 and DR-3 (one op on one target per edit event, so a regroup is several events); store schema at architecture.md:434: idem TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE.
findings.failure_scenario: Agent: `edit hide X --base 40`, then `edit undo E`, then `edit hide X --base 40` again. The third call returns replayed:true and X stays visible, while the agent believes it hid X. A retry of `edit group` killed after commit has to reconstruct a three-event reply from one key.
findings.proposed_fix: Key multi-event commands as `idem#n` per event, and store the full reply on the first event, so a replay returns it whole. Mark derived-key replays in the reply: `meta.replayed_from` names the original seq and the hint says 'pass a new --idem to repeat'. Alternatively, derive the key only for calls the engine knows are retries, such as the outbox and harness, and otherwise mint a fresh one.

findings.title: The fold isn't pure in (facts, events, at): claim and presence expiry read the wall clock, and cache keys may include values that change on every commit
findings.claim: Open claims (`until` timestamps) feed the fold's indexes and the reconciler's 'in progress' rule. Presence feeds `who`. Both depend on the current time, not on `at`, so fold(at=N) and reconcile aren't reproducible, and incremental_fold_equals_full_fold can flake across an expiry. Separately, the Jev cache key hashes canonical(state). If a slice serializes Evidence.commit or snapshot IDs, any commit invalidates every slice of that repo. That would re-ask decisions and re-deal card-only kinds on S7's routine rescan.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:354 ("pure and deterministic"); 361 (indexes include open claims); 938 (in progress = an item with an open claim); 424 (claims with an expiry); 823 (the cache key over canonical(state)); contracts.md Evidence {commit, branch}. KICKOFF S7: "0 Claude calls ... at most one card".
findings.failure_scenario: A replayed S4 run whose hand-off claim (30 min) expires mid-test classifies differently on the reconcile before and after the expiry. On S7, if dependency_real slices carry evidence commits, every storefront import edge with confidence below 1 gets a new input hash at the routine commit, which means a Jev call and a card each.
findings.proposed_fix: Pass `now` into the fold as an explicit input taken from the event or command, and record it in replays. Separate time-dependent overlays (claims, presence) from the pure model. Define slice canonicalization to drop commit, snapshot and seq values, keeping path, line and contains. Add a test that a no-op commit leaves every input hash unchanged.

verdicts.reason: Under the design as written, B's rename (agent:bbbbbbbb:chat) is a ghost. Revisions count only applied events, so a ghost never raises rev(target, field). The tab's later rename therefore applies with no conflict, which contradicts S8's assertion that the tab gets stale_write and the node keeps B's name. I found nothing in DR-4, DR-5, DR-7 or the write path that gives ghosts revision weight. The harness also never arranges for a person to write between an agent's read and its write, so the 'agent stale write' assertion has no producer either. Tier A S8 would fail, so the finding is material.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:368 says "rev(target, field) is the seq of the last applied event that set it". architecture.md:328 and DR-4 (decisions.md:151) say "any agent or model edit is a ghost". The write-path diagram (architecture.md:262-268) checks "a field this edit sets has a revision above base by another actor". feature_list.json:408 asserts "the tab's stale rename returned stale_write ... and the node still has B's name", and feature_list.json:397 sets B as PLANROOM_ACTOR=agent:bbbbbbbb:chat. contracts.md:228 says "edit ... any (agent writes are ghosts)".

verdicts.reason: The conflict test exempts writes by the same actor. Every canvas tab with a session cookie resolves to the same person:<os-user>, so two tabs on two devices can overwrite each other's fields from stale bases and get no conflict. R10 names that case and forbids last-writer-wins for user-authored state. One mitigation exists: contracts.md gives Actor::Person a `surface` field. If actor equality is structural, pane against tab would conflict, but tab against tab (both Surface::Canvas) still would not, and the docs never say whether surface counts toward equality. Every Bash agent without PLANROOM_ACTOR shares agent:cli, so one agent can reject another's ghosts as if they were its own. This is a material R10 and principle-1 violation.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:403: "A write conflicts when a field it sets has rev > base, written by a different actor". architecture.md:410: "An actor never conflicts with its own later writes." architecture.md:380: person:<os-user> for a TTY, the person key, or "a canvas request with a session cookie". architecture.md:382: "a CLI call with no TTY and no person key (agent:cli)". contracts.md:377: `Person { id, name, surface }`, with no tab or device ID. KICKOFF.md:89 (R10): "canvas tabs on several devices ... User-authored state is never last-writer-wins."

verdicts.reason: One sub-claim is weak: the last reconciled head can be derived from the previous `scan` event's commit, so a dedicated table is not strictly needed. The core gap is real. Facts exist only for head snapshots (snapshots.purpose has no per-commit variant), yet rule 1 needs a per-commit 'fact delta' that breaks a rule 'met before it'. The fixture builds worker's teammates branch from main at commit 09, before the hand-off, so at the audit commit's parent the forbid rule was not met. Taken literally, the audit commit doesn't qualify as a regression. Nothing defines how merge commits (from `git merge --no-ff teammates` and the hand-off's own `--no-ff` merge) are attributed or excluded. Rule 5 would classify any change unit 'not on a hand-off branch' as unplanned, and the hand-off merge commit sits on main. S4's reconciliation_after_merges is tier A, so this is material.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:933: "Change units are the commits between each repo's last reconciled head and its current head ... Each carries ... its fact delta". architecture.md:936: "breaks an intended rule that was met before it". architecture.md:940: unplanned means "not on a hand-off branch". architecture.md:439-441: snapshot purposes are head | link | proposed | runs | file only. examples/fixture/repos/worker/10-audit-rows/COMMIT.toml sets branch = "teammates", and build-fixture:218-224 says a branch "needs a main commit to start from". feature_list.json S4 step: "git -C $OUT/worker merge --no-ff teammates". Nothing in the docs mentions merge commits or first-parent handling.

verdicts.reason: The fold applies edits in seq order by effective status, and a review changes only status. An accepted ghost or a 'Use yours' resolution therefore takes effect at its original seq, under any applied write made in between. The reviewer's choice silently has no effect. The docs define no new edit event or fresh compare-and-set for an accept. 'Re-applies the edit with a fresh base' is the only hint, and it doesn't say the edit is re-sequenced. A person's action that changes nothing, with no report, violates principle 1 ('never lose or overwrite what someone did'), so this is material.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:359: "Apply every edit with effective status Applied ... in seq order". architecture.md:350: "An edit's status is set at commit time and changed later only by review and undo events". architecture.md:410: "Choosing 'yours' is a review accept that re-applies the edit with a fresh base". contracts.md:389: `Review { of: EventId, verdict }` carries no new edit payload. A ghost never raises rev (architecture.md:368), so Bob's intervening write applies cleanly.

verdicts.reason: The truth's evidence for OrdersHighErrorRate includes a Go `//` comment line. The extractor contract and contracts.md both forbid taking evidence from comments, and no extractor or linker is designed to attach that line. The design does keep a generic infeasibility-record fallback (architecture.md:54, R-3), but KICKOFF allows that only when a scenario is 'infeasible as written'. This item is feasible and excluded only by the design's own rule, so the fallback doesn't cover it. The comparator requires full evidence recall, so S2 (tier A) fails. Material.
verdicts.evidence: In TRUTH questions.observability.alerts[0].evidence[2], middleware.go line 26 contains "// Prometheus exporter publishes them as orders_http_requests_total and". architecture.md:513: "Code extractors take string literals and calls from syntax nodes, never from comments or docstrings". contracts.md:536: "code facts come from syntax nodes, never comments or docstrings". architecture.md:1198: "Full evidence recall is the bar". KICKOFF.md:134: infeasibility applies only "if one turns out to be infeasible as written". No mention of `_total` or OTel-to-Prometheus name mapping appears anywhere in the docs.

verdicts.reason: The release pack takes versions only from manifests and tags. Orders is Go, and go.mod carries no version. No extractor turns CHANGELOG headings into a repo version. The artifacts pack's `markdown` extractor makes section nodes but sets no version. Evidence requires a file path, a line and a verified line, so tag-derived and git-derived facts (tags, commits, co_change, owned_by) have no valid evidence and are dropped at ingest under 'evidence or nothing'. The stale answer for platform -> orders can't carry the required orders/CHANGELOG.md:7 evidence, and the history lens has nothing to show. S2 is tier A, so this is material.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:681: the release pack's extractors are "gh_workflow release triggers, manifests' versions; deploys linker". architecture.md:554: deploys joins "compose images, repo manifests and tags". architecture.md:512: "Every fact carries at least one Evidence whose contains is the exact source line ... drops any that fail". contracts.md:317-319: `Evidence { path, line: u32 ... }`, where line is required. TRUTH questions.stale_versions.stale[1].evidence[1]: orders/CHANGELOG.md line 7, "## [1.5.0] - 2026-09-22". A search for 'changelog' in the docs finds no extractor.

verdicts.reason: The canvas half is weaker than claimed. Pollers push frames only once every 200 ms data_version poll, so a 100 ms trailing debounce gets its quiet gap between batches and still refreshes. The mod half holds. Under sustained load a frame batch arrives every 200 ms, so '250 ms of quiet' never happens and the pane never refreshes until load stops. The mod's refresh runs `focus`, a one-shot command whose freshness check rescans any repo whose HEAD moved, so a redraw can wait on a full scan. The S8 gate measures only commit-to-frame latency, so it would pass while the pane is stale. That violates R10 ('every surface updates live') and S8's 'within 1 s'. Material.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:240: "After 250 ms of quiet the mod runs planroom focus --json". architecture.md:1051: "The stream polls PRAGMA data_version every 200 ms ... the canvas debounces 100 ms, the mod 250 ms". architecture.md:238: "Each command first checks freshness ... and rescans what moved". feature_list.json:406: "commit-to-SSE and commit-to-watch latency p99 under 1 s". KICKOFF.md:89 (R10): "every surface updates live".

verdicts.reason: `unmonitored` filters 'runtime containers', but no kind, prop or rule defines that term or excludes compose services that are observability infrastructure. The code pack's container kinds are service, datastore, queue, library and tooling. The observability pack contributes no container kind. Nothing says how the compose extractor classifies redis as queue, postgres as datastore, or otel-collector, prometheus and grafana as observability. As written, those three would come out as unwatched service containers, and the answer would not match TRUTH's four. S2 is tier A, so this is material.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:652 and 663: "filter runtime containers without incoming watches". architecture.md:678 lists the code pack kinds, with no observability-infra kind. architecture.md:680 lists observability kinds as alert, dashboard, panel, metric and collector_pipeline. architecture.md:621: "Services with no repo (redis, orders-db) sit under the workspace", with no kind stated. TRUTH questions.unmonitored.answer = [storefront, worker, redis, orders-db], and out_of_scope.observability_infrastructure = [otel-collector, prometheus, grafana].

verdicts.reason: This is real, and the reviewer's 'minor' rating is right. The freshness-check rescan is described without taking the scan:REPO lease. The snapshot UNIQUE constraint isn't paired with an upsert. Leases are bare expiring rows with no epoch checked at commit. The result is a duplicate or failed rescan, or a duplicated decision event, which is untidy but not data loss or a guaranteed acceptance failure.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:161: duties run under leases, but with no live process the work "runs inline ... in the next command's freshness check". architecture.md:238: every command "rescans what moved", with no lease mentioned. architecture.md:439-441: `UNIQUE (repo, commit_id, purpose, packs_hash)`. architecture.md:450: `leases (name, holder, expires_at)`, with no epoch.

verdicts.reason: This is real, and 'minor' is right. The preflight covers merge conflicts but not the process dying between the per-repo `git merge` calls. The order of the `merged` event and the git merges is unspecified. Replays return a stored reply regardless of repo state. So the 'nothing is ever half-merged' claim doesn't survive a crash. The git state stays recoverable, so this is not material.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:984: "Only if every repo passes does it run git merge --no-ff planroom/KEY in each ... so nothing is ever half-merged across repos". DR-8 (decisions.md): "Same key and hash: the stored reply with meta.replayed: true". architecture.md:152: watch "dies on reload ... by design [mod-api §7]". The docs define no intermediate `merging` step.

verdicts.reason: This is real, and 'minor' is right. A derived key over (actor, command, args, base) makes a deliberate repeat with the same base after an undo collide with the first call, and the repeat silently replays. `idem` is UNIQUE per event row, but commands that write several events (a regroup, a multi-repo scan, a decision plus its effects) have no rule for deriving one key per event, or for storing and replaying the whole reply.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:416: "the engine derives sha256(actor ‖ command ‖ canonical(args) ‖ base)". architecture.md:434: `idem TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE` on events. architecture.md:349: "one of three operations (put, set, retract) on one target", so multi-target commands write several events. architecture.md:237: a scan "appends one scan event per repo".

verdicts.reason: The claim-and-presence half is real. The fold indexes open claims, and the reconciler's 'in progress' rule depends on them, but claim expiry uses wall-clock `until` timestamps, so fold(at) is not a pure function of (facts, events, at). The cache half is speculative. A decision kind's slice declares an explicit `fields` list (architecture.md:742), which probably keeps commit values out of the input hash, although canonicalization is never spelled out. Overall this is minor, as rated.

An item with an open claim". contracts.md: `Claim { target, until: Timestamp, release }`. architecture.md:742: `slice = { query = "neighbors", relations = [...], fields = ["name", "props.done_test"] }`. architecture.md:730: input hash = sha256 of the kind, its version, the questions and the serialized slice.
